title: Exodus Chapter 24 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 24 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 24 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 24.

questions.question: Who were instructed to come up unto the LORD along with Moses in Exodus 24?
options: Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:1 states that Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel were to come up unto the LORD.

questions.question: According to Exodus 24, who alone was allowed to come near the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses alone
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:2 specifies that Moses alone shall come near the LORD, but they shall not come nigh.

questions.question: What was the people's response when Moses told them all the words of the LORD?
options: All the words which the LORD hath said will we do
We will consider and reply later
We cannot obey all the LORD's words
Only some of the words will we do
questions.correctAnswer: All the words which the LORD hath said will we do
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:3 records the people answered with one voice saying they will do all the words which the LORD hath said.

questions.question: What did Moses build under the hill after writing all the words of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: An altar and twelve pillars
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:4 states Moses built an altar under the hill and twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel.

questions.question: Who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of oxen unto the LORD?
options: Young men of the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Young men of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:5 explains that young men of the children of Israel offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of oxen unto the LORD.

questions.question: What did Moses do with half of the blood from the offerings?
questions.correctAnswer: Put it in basons
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:6 states Moses took half of the blood and put it in basons.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was instructed that all the people could come up with him near the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:2 clearly states that Moses alone shall come near the LORD; neither shall the people go up with him.

questions.question: True or False: The people responded unanimously that they would obey all the words of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:3 records that all the people answered with one voice, saying they will do all the words which the LORD hath said.

questions.question: Which of the following was built by Moses early in the morning according to Exodus 24?
questions.correctAnswer: An altar and twelve pillars
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:4 mentions Moses arose early in the morning and built an altar and twelve pillars.

questions.question: What type of offerings were sacrificed to the LORD by the young men?
options: Burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:5 specifies that burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen were offered unto the LORD by the young men.

questions.question: True or False: Moses sprinkled all the blood on the altar.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:6 shows Moses took half of the blood and put it in basons and sprinkled the other half on the altar.

questions.question: In Exodus 24, which instruction comes first?
options: Moses and others to come up unto the LORD and worship afar off
Moses alone to come near the LORD
The people to offer burnt offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and others to come up unto the LORD and worship afar off
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:1 is the first instruction where Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders are told to come up and worship afar off, before the other actions.

questions.question: Who was not allowed to come near the LORD according to Exodus 24?
questions.correctAnswer: The people
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:2 states the people shall not come nigh nor go up with Moses to the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Moses took all the blood and sprinkled it on the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:6 shows Moses took half of the blood and sprinkled it on the altar; he sprinkled the other half on the people later (verse 8).

questions.question: What did Moses do after writing all the words of the LORD?
options: Built an altar and twelve pillars under the hill
Went up alone to the mount
Read the book of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Built an altar and twelve pillars under the hill
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:4 reveals that Moses wrote all the words, then early in the morning built an altar and twelve pillars.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 24 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 24 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the people say after Moses read the book of the covenant to them?
options: All that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient
We will question the LORD's commands
We will wait for further instructions
questions.correctAnswer: All that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:7 records that the people responded to Moses reading the book of the covenant by saying, 'All that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient.' This shows their commitment to obey God's commands.

questions.question: What did Moses do with the blood after the covenant was read to the people?
options: He sprinkled it on the people
He poured it on the ground
He kept it in a jar
He gave it to the elders
questions.correctAnswer: He sprinkled it on the people
questions.explanation: According to Exodus 24:8, Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people, declaring it as the blood of the covenant that the LORD had made concerning the words they had accepted.

questions.question: Who accompanied Moses when he went up to see God, according to Exodus 24?
options: Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:9 specifies that Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel to see God, illustrating the select group allowed near God’s presence.

questions.question: What did Moses and the elders see under the feet of God?
options: A paved work of sapphire stone, like the body of heaven in clearness
questions.correctAnswer: A paved work of sapphire stone, like the body of heaven in clearness
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:10 describes that under God's feet was something like a paved work of sapphire stone, resembling the clear expanse of heaven, symbolizing God's majestic glory.

questions.question: Did God lay His hand upon the nobles of Israel when they saw Him?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:11 states that God did not lay His hand upon the nobles of Israel; they saw God and still ate and drank, indicating His blessing and acceptance of them.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise to give Moses on the mount?
options: Tables of stone, a law, and commandments which He had written
questions.correctAnswer: Tables of stone, a law, and commandments which He had written
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:12 records that God told Moses to come up the mount to receive tables of stone, a law, and commandments written by God Himself, which Moses would then teach the people.

questions.question: How does Exodus 24 teach about obedience through the people's response to the covenant?
options: It shows the importance of agreeing to God's commands wholeheartedly
It shows that people do not need to obey immediately
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of agreeing to God's commands wholeheartedly
questions.explanation: The people’s unified response in Exodus 24:7, 'All that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient,' demonstrates wholehearted commitment to obey God, highlighting faith and trust as foundational virtues.

questions.question: What does the sprinkling of blood on the people symbolize in the context of Exodus 24?
options: The blood of the covenant made between God and Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The blood of the covenant made between God and Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:8 explains that the blood Moses sprinkled on the people was the blood of the covenant, symbolizing the solemn agreement and commitment between God and Israel.

questions.question: According to Exodus 24, what practical lesson about leadership can we learn from Moses sending young men to offer sacrifices?
options: Delegating responsibilities in worship and service is important
Leaders must do all tasks themselves
questions.correctAnswer: Delegating responsibilities in worship and service is important
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:5 shows Moses sending young men to offer burnt and peace offerings, indicating that effective leadership includes delegation and involving others in service to God.

questions.question: What does Exodus 24:11 teach about the relationship between God and His people?
options: God's favor allows His people to experience fellowship and blessing
God punishes all who see Him
questions.correctAnswer: God's favor allows His people to experience fellowship and blessing
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:11 indicates that the nobles saw God, were not harmed, and ate and drank in His presence, showing a close and blessed fellowship with God based on His favor.

questions.question: How does the cloud covering Mount Sinai in Exodus 24:15-16 symbolize God's presence and majesty?
options: It represents God's glory and the mystery surrounding His revelation
It is a sign to leave the mountain
questions.correctAnswer: It represents God's glory and the mystery surrounding His revelation
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:15-16 describes the cloud covering the mount and the glory of the LORD abiding there, symbolizing God's majestic presence and the awe-inspiring mystery of His revelation to Moses.

questions.question: What promise does Exodus 24:12 give to those who follow God's commands as presented in the preceding verses?
options: They will receive God's law and commandments to guide them
They will be free from all troubles immediately
They will become rulers over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive God's law and commandments to guide them
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:12 promises that God will give Moses tables of stone with law and commandments, implying that obedience leads to receiving divine guidance for living.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was accompanied by Joshua when he went up the mount of God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:13 clearly states that Moses rose up along with his minister Joshua and went up into the mount of God together.

questions.question: What instruction did Moses give to the elders while he and Joshua went up the mount?
options: To wait for them and consult Aaron and Hur if needed
To follow him immediately up the mount
questions.correctAnswer: To wait for them and consult Aaron and Hur if needed
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:14 records Moses instructing the elders to stay put and consult Aaron and Hur for any matters until Moses and Joshua returned, showing wise delegation and order.

questions.question: True or False: The sight of the glory of the LORD was described as gentle and comforting on the mount.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:17 describes the glory of the LORD as like devouring fire on the mount’s top, which indicates a powerful and fearsome presence rather than gentle comfort.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 24 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 24.

questions.question: Who accompanied Moses when he went up into the mount of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:13 states that Moses rose up with his minister Joshua and went up into the mount of God.

questions.question: What instruction did Moses give to the elders before ascending the mount?
options: Tarry here until we come again
questions.correctAnswer: Tarry here until we come again
questions.explanation: According to Exodus 24:14, Moses told the elders to tarry there until he and Joshua returned.

questions.question: Who were left with the elders to address matters during Moses' absence?
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and Hur
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:14 specifies that Aaron and Hur were left with the elders to handle any matters.

questions.question: What phenomenon covered Mount Sinai when Moses ascended?
questions.correctAnswer: A cloud
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:15 states that a cloud covered the mount when Moses ascended.

questions.question: How many days did the glory of the LORD remain upon Mount Sinai, covered by the cloud?
questions.correctAnswer: Six days
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:16 says the glory of the LORD abode on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days.

questions.question: On which day did the LORD call Moses out of the midst of the cloud?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventh day
questions.explanation: According to Exodus 24:16, the LORD called Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud.

questions.question: How was the sight of the glory of the LORD described to the children of Israel?
options: Like devouring fire on the top of the mount
Like a peaceful cloud covering the land
Like a rainbow in the sky
questions.correctAnswer: Like devouring fire on the top of the mount
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:17 describes the glory of the LORD as like devouring fire on the mount's top in the eyes of Israel.

questions.question: How long was Moses in the mount during this period?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty days and forty nights
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:18 clearly states Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights.

questions.question: True or False: The elders saw the God of Israel and ate and drank in His presence.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:11 notes the elders saw God and did eat and drink, showing a unique fellowship with Him.

questions.question: True or False: Moses sprinkled the blood of the covenant only on the altar, not on the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:8 shows Moses sprinkled the blood on the people as well as the altar, symbolizing the covenant.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of Moses’ forty days on the mountain?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 4:1-2
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:1-2 records Jesus fasting for forty days and nights in the wilderness, echoing Moses’ time on the mount (Exodus 24:18) as a period of testing and preparation.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the description of the cloud covering the mount for six days and the LORD calling on the seventh day?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:16 shows inclusio, framing the sacred event with the six days of cloud and the seventh day of divine communication, emphasizing holiness and completion.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'covenant' in this chapter?
options: Berith - a binding agreement or treaty
questions.correctAnswer: Berith - a binding agreement or treaty
questions.explanation: The word for 'covenant' here is 'Berith,' meaning a binding agreement, which fits the covenantal context of blood sprinkled on altar and people (Exodus 24:8).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with the theme of the 'blood of the covenant' in Exodus 24:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 9:15
questions.explanation: Hebrews 9:15 speaks of Jesus as mediator of a new covenant, referencing the significance of blood in covenantal terms, paralleling Exodus 24:8.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is closely related to the theophany (appearance of God) described in Exodus 24:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 1:26-28
questions.explanation: Ezekiel’s vision of God’s radiant glory (Ezekiel 1:26-28) parallels the description of God’s appearance on the sapphire pavement in Exodus 24:10.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 24 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 24 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the sprinkling of blood on both the altar and the people in Exodus 24 signify theologically?
options: The establishment of a covenant relationship between God and Israel
A symbol of God’s wrath against sin
A ceremony of purification from physical impurity
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of a covenant relationship between God and Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:6-8 shows Moses taking the blood and sprinkling it on the altar and the people, declaring it as the blood of the covenant God made concerning all His words. This act signifies covenant ratification, a key theological theme of divine promise and human obedience (cf. Hebrews 9:18-22).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly emphasized by the description of the glory of the LORD as a 'devouring fire' on the mount?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness and justice
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:17 depicts the LORD’s glory as a devouring fire, symbolizing His holiness that consumes sin and His righteous judgment. This imagery communicates God’s purity and justice toward His covenant people (cf. Isaiah 6:6-7).

questions.question: How does the presence of the seventy elders with Moses on the mountain relate to Israel’s corporate sanctification?
options: It represents the shared responsibility of leadership in covenant mediation
It was a social gathering without theological significance
It was a requirement for legal witnesses only
It ensured the elders’ exemption from the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the shared responsibility of leadership in covenant mediation
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:1 and 9 describe seventy elders accompanying Moses, symbolizing collective leadership and the corporate nature of Israel’s covenant relationship with God. This reflects the theological principle that sanctification and covenant participation are communal (cf. Numbers 11:16-17).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by the people's unified response, 'All the words which the LORD hath said will we do'?
options: The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of covenant obedience
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:3 records the people’s unanimous commitment to obey all the LORD’s words, emphasizing the covenantal principle that God’s people respond to divine revelation with obedience, foundational in biblical covenant theology (cf. Deuteronomy 29:9-13).

questions.question: Which theological significance does the building of twelve pillars under the hill have?
options: It symbolizes the unity and identity of the twelve tribes under God’s covenant
It was a purely architectural decision with no symbolic meaning
It represented twelve different gods worshiped by Israel
It was intended to mark Israel’s territory geographically
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the unity and identity of the twelve tribes under God’s covenant
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:4 mentions Moses building twelve pillars, corresponding to the twelve tribes. This signifies corporate identity and unity under the covenant, reflecting Israel’s collective relationship to God (cf. Genesis 49).

questions.question: What aspect of God’s character is revealed by Him not laying His hand upon the nobles of Israel during their vision of Him?
options: God’s mercy and graciousness toward His covenant people
God’s omnipotence in restraining His power
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy and graciousness toward His covenant people
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:11 states that God did not lay His hand on the nobles, demonstrating His mercy and grace in allowing them to behold His presence without immediate judgment, affirming His covenantal kindness (cf. Psalm 103:8).

questions.question: How does Moses’ ascent into the mount for forty days and nights prefigure Christ’s role in redemptive history?
options: It typifies Christ’s role as mediator and intercessor between God and humanity
It foreshadows Christ’s rejection by Israel
It symbolizes the legalistic works of the law
It predicts Christ’s earthly ministry duration
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies Christ’s role as mediator and intercessor between God and humanity
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:18 depicts Moses’ prolonged communion with God, a typology of Christ as the ultimate mediator who intercedes on behalf of His people, bridging God and humanity (cf. Hebrews 9:11-15).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do verses 5-6 and 11 convey about the nature of God’s covenant and presence?
options: God’s covenant involves sacrificial blood and His holy presence can be experienced by His people
God’s covenant is symbolic only and His presence is invisible
God’s covenant excludes the elders and His presence is punitive
God’s covenant demands isolation and His presence is unapproachable
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant involves sacrificial blood and His holy presence can be experienced by His people
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 emphasize the sacrificial ritual (blood on altar), while verse 11 reveals that the elders saw God and ate/drank with Him, indicating covenant fellowship with a holy God. Together, these reveal covenant ratification and relational presence (cf. Leviticus 17:11, Psalm 34:8).

questions.question: How does Exodus 24:12 contribute to the doctrine of divine revelation?
options: It shows God giving Moses written law and commandments for teaching the people
It denies any written form of God’s law
It suggests that revelation is only oral and secret
It implies that law is unnecessary for the people
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God giving Moses written law and commandments for teaching the people
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:12 illustrates God’s initiative to provide Moses with stone tablets containing law and commandments, revealing God’s self-disclosure in written form for instruction, foundational to biblical revelation (cf. Deuteronomy 5:22).

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by Moses’ instruction to the elders to wait with Aaron and Hur for matters to be addressed?
options: Delegated leadership and orderly governance in God’s covenant community
Immediate resolution of all issues by Moses personally
The absence of any human intermediary
questions.correctAnswer: Delegated leadership and orderly governance in God’s covenant community
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:14 records Moses instructing elders to stay with Aaron and Hur, highlighting the principle of shared leadership and orderly administration within the community under God’s covenant (cf. Acts 6:1-6).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the vivid theophany described in Exodus 24:10-11 is mythological and not a real encounter. What does Exodus 24:10-11 actually teach about God’s revelation to His people?
options: God’s presence can be tangibly experienced by His covenant people without harm
God is only accessible through dreams
God’s presence is unknowable and invisible
God never reveals Himself directly to humans
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence can be tangibly experienced by His covenant people without harm
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:10-11 affirms that Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and elders saw God’s glory and shared a meal with Him, indicating a genuine, tangible divine encounter granted to covenant members, countering sceptical claims (cf. Genesis 32:30, John 1:18).

questions.question: What does Exodus 24:15-16 reveal about God’s transcendence and immanence in the context of Mount Sinai?
options: God’s glory both covers the mount in a cloud (transcendence) and calls Moses from within it (immanence)
God is absent and silent during the cloud covering
God’s presence is limited to physical space
God hides from His people permanently
questions.correctAnswer: God’s glory both covers the mount in a cloud (transcendence) and calls Moses from within it (immanence)
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:15-16 describes a cloud covering the mount (signifying God’s overwhelming holiness and otherness) while simultaneously God calls Moses from inside it, illustrating the paradox of divine transcendence and immanence (cf. Psalm 97:2).

questions.question: Which doctrine is underscored by Moses writing all the words of the LORD and building an altar with twelve pillars?
options: The doctrine of covenant ratification and remembrance
The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of predestined election without human response
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of covenant ratification and remembrance
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:4 shows Moses writing the LORD’s words and erecting an altar and twelve pillars, symbolizing formal ratification of the covenant and memorializing God’s promises to the tribes, teaching covenant faithfulness (cf. Joshua 24:26-27).

questions.question: How does Exodus 24:13 demonstrate the role of Joshua in the covenant community?
options: Joshua serves as Moses’ minister and successor, implying continuity in God’s leadership
Joshua is excluded from covenant participation
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua serves as Moses’ minister and successor, implying continuity in God’s leadership
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:13 identifies Joshua as Moses’ minister accompanying him, signaling his role as a faithful assistant and future leader, underscoring God’s providential preparation for covenant continuity (cf. Deuteronomy 31:7-8).

questions.question: What synthesis of theological truths emerges from the people's covenant commitment (verse 3) and Moses reading the book of the covenant (verse 7)?
options: The people's verbal commitment is affirmed by public, formal covenant reading establishing obedience
The people reject God’s laws after hearing them
The covenant is secret and unspoken
The covenant is only between Moses and God, excluding the people
questions.correctAnswer: The people's verbal commitment is affirmed by public, formal covenant reading establishing obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 7 together show the people’s vocal promise to obey and their reaffirmation upon hearing the covenant read aloud, indicating public covenant ratification and the doctrine of covenant obedience (cf. Nehemiah 8:1-6).
